intro.caption: Lesson 2-8 — the mean. Clip Squad enters Fair Share Showdown, a live creator game show hosted by Max Maxwell. Level the data stacks, find the mean, and balance the final round!

balloons.t: Welcome to Fair Share Showdown! Four creators, four uneven stacks. Who knows the REAL average?
Watch out! Max loves trick questions!
My stacks are 2, 5, 14, 7, 12! The middle stack is 14, so the mean is 14! Replay!
Wrong! The mean is the FAIR SHARE — add all five, then share equally by 5!

pages.caption: The mean is the fair-share average: combine every value into one total, then divide equally by how many values there are.

balloons.t: Move cubes from tall stacks to short stacks until every stack matches. That height is the mean!
Scoreboard's hot! Add up every value, then divide by the count!
Do not stop at the total! Dividing is what makes it a mean.
The mean is also a balance point! Total above the mean must equal total below.
Or multiply target mean × count to get the needed total, then subtract what we have!
Final round! Solve my mystery score AND prove whether a mean must be in the list!
We know the total rule and the balance rule. Let's win this trophy.
Every stack leveled, trophy won, and Dex finally knows the mean is NOT the middle!

win.caption: Whether you level the stacks, add and divide, or balance distances above and below, you always land on the same mean.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Level the Stacks
gates.prompt: Use the fair-share model to level the stacks and bust Dex's middle-number claim.
hints: Conceptual: leveling the stacks gives every group the exact same amount without changing the total.
Procedural: add all the values to find the total cubes, then divide by the number of stacks.

steps: Share equally among 4 stacks: 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cubes per stack.
worked.q: What is the fair share of 3, 5, 10?

items.label: Four clips got 6, 10, 8, and 12 comments. Fair share per clip:
items.aria: mean number of comments per clip

fb.msg: 36 is the total comments. You still need to share equally among the 4 clips!
Check the total: 6 + 10 + 8 + 12 = 36. Now divide 36 by 4.
If every clip had 10, the total would be 40, not 36.

items.q: Dex says the mean of 2, 5, 14, 7, 12 is 14 because 14 is in the middle. Why is he wrong?

options.t: He forgot to sort first; the mean is 7
options.fb: 7 is the median (middle after sorting), not the mean. The mean is 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

options.t: Mean is the fair-share average (add all 5, divide by 5), not the middle number
He should average only the first and last numbers
options.fb: Using only 2 and 12 ignores the other three values in the data set.

options.t: The mean is always the biggest number
options.fb: A fair share sits between the smallest and largest values.

gates.pass: 9 comments per clip, and Dex's 14-in-the-middle theory is officially retired!

gates.title: Gate 2 · Find the Mean
gates.prompt: Compute the mean of each data set on the game-show scoreboard.
hints: Conceptual: the mean is the typical value if the total were shared equally across every item.
Procedural: sum all the values in the data set, then divide by the count of values.

items.label: Mean of 14, 18, 12, 16, 20:

fb.msg: 80 is the sum! Divide by 5 (the number of values) to get the mean.
12 is just the middle position of the unsorted list. Add all 5 and divide by 5.
Count carefully: there are 5 values, not 4. Divide 80 by 5.

items.fbDefault: Add all 5 numbers (80), then divide by 5.

items.label: Clip Squad earned 60 new fans total over 4 streams. Mean fans per stream:
items.aria: mean fans per stream for 60 fans over 4 streams

fb.msg: Don't add 60 + 4. Share the 60 fans equally across 4 streams by dividing.
60 × 4 would be 60 fans on EACH stream. You want 60 shared across 4 streams.

items.fbDefault: Divide the total 60 fans by 4 streams.

gates.pass: 16 and 15! The scoreboard lights up teal across the studio.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Find the Missing Value
gates.prompt: Work backward from a target mean using the total or the balance-point rule.
hints: Conceptual: if you know the target mean and how many values there are, you know the exact total needed (or balance above and below).
Procedural: multiply target mean × total count to find the needed total, then subtract the values you already have.

steps: Example: target mean of 10 over 3 games. First two games are 8 and 9.
worked.q: Target mean is 20 over 3 games. First two are 18 and 21. Game 3?

items.label: Nova wants a mean of 15 likes over 4 clips. Her first 3 clips got 12, 18, and 14. Likes needed on clip 4:
items.aria: likes needed on clip 4 to reach mean 15

fb.msg: If clip 4 got 15, the total would be 59, not 60! The mean would be less than 15.
44 is the sum of the first 3 clips. Subtract 44 from the target total of 60.

items.q: Using balance point for a target mean of 15, three clips are 3 below, 3 above, and 1 below. Where must clip 4 sit?

options.fb: That puts 5 below and only 3 above — the scale tips down!
Then there are 4 below and 3 above — still 1 short!
3 + 4 = 7 above vs 4 below — that tips the scale too high!

gates.pass: 16 likes — 4 below balanced by 4 above! Clip Squad moves to the final round.

gates.title: Boss Gate · The Final Round
gates.prompt: Solve all three final-round challenges to win Fair Share Showdown.
hints: Conceptual: the mean is the fair share (total ÷ count) and does not have to appear in the data list.
Procedural: add and divide for a mean; multiply target mean × count and subtract known values for a missing value.

steps: Example: target mean 15 over 4 rounds; first three are 12, 15, 14.
worked.q: Target mean 10 over 4 rounds; first three are 8, 11, 9. Round 4?

items.label: Lock 1 · Mean of 22, 18, 25, 15, 20:

fb.msg: 100 is the sum of all 5 numbers. Divide 100 by 5!
25 is just the middle position in the unsorted list, not the mean.

items.fbDefault: Add all 5 numbers (100), then divide by 5.

items.label: Lock 2 · Target mean is 12 over 5 rounds. First 4 rounds are 10, 14, 9, 11. Score needed in round 5:
items.aria: score needed in round 5 for mean 12 over 5 rounds

fb.msg: The first 4 rounds total 44, which is 4 below 48. Round 5 must make up that 4!
44 is the sum of the first 4 rounds. Subtract 44 from 12 × 5 = 60.

items.q: Lock 3 · Does the mean always have to be one of the numbers in the data set?

options.t: Yes — the mean must appear in the list
options.fb: Check 4 and 6: their mean is 5, which is not in the list!

options.t: Yes — because the mean is the middle number
options.fb: The mean is the fair share, not the middle value, and it need not be in the list.

options.t: No — for example, the mean of 4 and 6 is 5, which is not in the list
No — the mean is always larger than every number
options.fb: A fair share always sits between the smallest and largest values.

gates.pass: 20, 16, and NO! Confetti rains down — Clip Squad sweeps Fair Share Showdown!

journal.heading: Lesson 2-8 — what the game show taught us
rows: Add every value to get the total, then divide by how many values there are: Mean = Total ÷ Count.
The total distance above the mean equals the total distance below the mean.
Multiply target mean × count to get the needed total, then subtract the known values.
The mean is not the middle number in an unsorted list, and it does not have to be one of the data values.
journal.quote: "Level the stacks first, talk trash second." — Blink

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 2-8 (Describe Data Using the Mean) as one focused read. Covers mean as fair share, mean as balance point, computing the mean, and finding a missing value from a target mean.
standards: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context using measures of center (mean)
